name: intraday_rsi_divergence_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Bullish/bearish RSI divergence on 1-min charts (price makes new low/high but RSI doesn't) signals exhaustion of the current micro-move. This works because momentum is decelerating even as price extends, typically caused by one-sided retail flow hitting diminishing institutional absorption. The pattern is well-known on daily charts but under-utilized on 1-min because visual divergence detection is hard to automate. A systematic detector with strict quantitative criteria captures this edge.
stock_filter: top 40 FnO stocks by avg daily turnover, exclude stocks with avg spread > 0.08%

conditions: rsi_at_swing_low > rsi_at_prev_swing_low (higher low in RSI = bullish divergence)
close > swing_low_price (price bouncing off the new low)
long.confirmation: close > open on signal bar (green candle at divergence low)

conditions: rsi_at_swing_high < rsi_at_prev_swing_high (lower high in RSI = bearish divergence)
short.confirmation: close < open on signal bar (red candle at divergence high)

exit.target: 0.4% from entry or midpoint of the prior swing range

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: none — divergence is a counter-trend signal by nature
other_filters: minimum 15 bars between swing points for valid divergence

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — pattern is well-known but hard to automate, keeping competition low

weaknesses: Swing point detection on 1-min is noisy — many false divergences in choppy markets
Lower win rate (52%) means long losing streaks are possible, testing risk limits
Divergence can persist for 50+ bars before resolving — time stop may cut winners short
prior_art: RSI divergence — classic Wilder-era concept. Systematic 1-min implementation is less common.
notes: Consider using a more robust swing detection algorithm (e.g., fractals or ZigZag indicator).
